head: f2484ec7e5001fed5dfcf0e809e88e90c8402328
classification_reasons: Spec tightness: tight going into build - spec.md's one flagged concern (inherited ZeroDivisionError message) was closed by the owner in phase b, both intent.md open questions are answered, and Acceptance is measurable (percent(1,4)==25.0, percent(7,100)==7.0, pytest.raises(ZeroDivisionError), '5 passed', silent compileall, 'All checks passed!').

Blast radius is small: the diff touches exactly the 3 files plan.md names (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py), all additive; no schema, contract, configuration or migration change; no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) in the diff; none of sdlc.yaml's risk_list items (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) is touched.

Test coverage: percent did not exist before this change, so no pre-existing test covered the code the plan added - the third routine criterion ('code the existing tests already cover') fails on its own terms even though the build adds its own tests in the same change, so this stays non-routine (iterations already at the cap of 2).
attempted: Intent: re-checked the build's actual diff against intent.md's Proposed outcome - percent(part, whole) added, percent(1,4)==25.0, zero whole raises ZeroDivisionError, exported in __init__.py and __all__, tests added for normal + zero case, add/divide untouched. No scope drift: the implementation is exactly what intent.md and spec.md describe, nothing extra, nothing missing.

Spec and plan: diffed sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py against plan.md's Order of work verbatim - step 1's exact function body (`return divide(part * 100, whole)`), step 2's import/__all__ edit, and step 3's two test names/assertions all match the plan byte-for-byte. Commit order matches the plan (steps 1+2 in one commit '4d78c1a', step 3 in 'be93afd', step 4's command run recorded in verifier.md at 'f2484ec'), and step 1+2 landing together matches the plan's own note that __init__.py would otherwise import a name that doesn't exist yet. No plan.md deviation, so no plan.md update was needed in this build commit.

Proof: ran all three project commands myself from repo root - `python -m compileall -q .` exit 0, no output; `python -m pytest` exit 0, 'tests/test_calc.py ....' + 'tests/test_flag.py .' + '5 passed in 0.01s'; `python -m ruff check .` exit 0, 'All checks passed!'. This matches verifier.md's recorded output and CLAUDE.md's stated healthy output exactly - the evidence is real toolchain output, not just a claim. Also independently checked the exact-percentage arithmetic (percent(7,100), percent(29,100), percent(57,100) all land on the exact integer float, confirming the scale-before-divide formula from spec.md/plan.md is what's actually in calc.py, not the round-1 rejected divide-then-scale order.

Blast radius: percent is new and additive; nothing else imports or calls it yet. divide is called, not modified, and its signature/behaviour are unchanged (confirmed by the diff and by `divide(10,4)`/`divide(1,0)` behaving as before). __all__ is appended to, not reordered, so add/divide's existing callers and tests are unaffected. git status shows one anomaly - 'M .env' in the working tree - but this is uncommitted, outside the change folder, a pre-existing sandbox artifact (git reports it as 'unsupported file type', consistent with a bubblewrap-mounted special file rather than a text edit), not part of this HEAD's diff, and not something this build touched or read (.env is on the Read deny list and was never opened).

Policies: coding-standards rule 2 (percent has no docstring, matching add/divide's style) and rule 7 (small, explicit function, no dead code) hold in the actual diff; rule 4's 'test that fails without it' holds specifically because test_percent asserts percent(7,100)==7.0, which the rejected divide-then-scale order would fail. security-baseline, data-conventions and ux-conventions still don't apply to this diff - pure arithmetic, no endpoint, no stored data, no UI. No new dependency was added (pyproject.toml untouched).

Tests: read tests/test_calc.py - test_percent and test_percent_zero_whole_raises are real pytest tests (plain assert / pytest.raises, no fixtures), not stubs, and they do exercise the exact-percentage edge case that would catch the round-1 defect if it were reintroduced. Pre-existing tests (test_add, test_divide_by_zero_raises) and tests/test_flag.py are untouched in the diff - confirmed no pre-existing test file was weakened, and change_type is 'feature' (not 'fix') so the fix-type test-lock rule doesn't apply here anyway.
